allergens.description: The allergens this product contains or may contain, as stated on the pack, ingredient list or allergen declaration, such as milk, nuts, peanuts, soy, gluten/wheat, egg, sesame, fish or shellfish, including 'may contain traces of' warnings. Return the list of allergens found; return [] if none are declared or the product has no ingredients that are allergens.

targeted_problems.description: The specific problem or health goal the product is designed to treat, relieve, prevent, control, support or measure. It spans baby and maternal needs; skin, hair and oral problems; nutrition and medical goals; device-based monitoring or relief; household stains, grease, pests, odour, leaks and wear; and pet health or grooming problems. The product’s stated function must connect directly to the named concern. Category membership or generic comfort, freshness and wellness language is insufficient.

wellness_goals.description: The health goal a food or drink is bought for in health drinks, teas, breakfast cereals and functional snacks: immunity, gut health, energy, sugar control or weight management (e.g. Kapiva juices for sugar control, Epigamia probiotic curd for gut health, Bournvita for energy). Not applicable for: everyday staples like Fortune sunflower oil or India Gate basmati rice that make no health claim.

craft_processes.description: A traditional, artisanal or specialised making process that is a central reason to choose the product. It includes bilona ghee, cold- or wood-pressed oils, stone-ground flour and slow-roasted foods; hand-carved or hand-rolled decor and incense; handloom or hand-block-printed furnishings; and handcrafted serveware or pre-seasoned cast-iron cookware. This describes how the item is made or prepared, rather than its material, geographic origin or the producer’s size.

value_explanations.bilona: A traditional method of making ghee by churning curd into butter, then heating the butter.

material_safety_claims.description: An explicit safety or suitability claim about the material, dye, coating or finish of a physical product. Examples include BPA-free bottles and pet bowls, food-grade kitchenware or silicone teethers, non-toxic toys, azo-free textiles, and rust-proof food-contact finishes. This concerns what an object is made of or treated with, rather than ingredients omitted from a food, cleaner or care formulation, which belong to clean_ingredient. General performance claims such as waterproof or anti-slip are different attributes.

value_explanations.azo_free: A stated exclusion of azo dyes from the product’s material or colouring.

distinctive_formats.description: A meaningful departure from the normal delivery, usage, build, texture or pack format of the product type in India. It includes food pouches, concentrates and baked snacks; patches, foams and roll-ons in care; supplement gummies or oral strips; detergent pods and sheets; unusual decor or furnishing formats; silicone kitchen tools; cordless or rechargeable devices; and lickable pet treats. Novelty is judged against the relevant shelf, so an established format or routine flavour, scent, shade or container extension is insufficient.

value_explanations.bldc: A brushless direct-current motor format, when different from the shelf norm.

d2c_brand.description: A brand created primarily as an online or direct-to-consumer business that still sells mainly through its own digital channels or online marketplaces rather than conventional retail. This describes the brand’s route to market across food, care, household goods, apparel or electronics, without implying premium pricing. An established mass-retail brand, marketplace reseller or white-label storefront does not qualify merely because it also sells online.

portability_upgrade.description: A design or pack feature that makes a product meaningfully easier to carry or use while travelling, outdoors or on the go than its shelf’s usual alternative. Examples include portable baby-care kits, single-serve foods or supplements, pocket care products, cordless lighting, travel pillows and towels, leak-proof travel drinkware, foldable or travel-lock devices, and pet carriers or drinking systems. Functional travel suitability matters; a product does not qualify solely because it is small or sample-sized.
